in_text_mentions: Histopathologically, sebaceous carcinoma is usually an ill-defined neoplasm with a nodular, lobular, or diffusely infiltrative architecture extending into the dermis and subcutaneous tissue [39] (Figure 3). Circumscription and pushing borders are uncommon but have been described, and an epidermal connection may be present. Periocular tumours and a subset of tumours occurring on genital areas may show characteristic pagetoid intraepithelial spread with single cells or small nests replacing the epidermis [36,40] (Figure 4). The tumour is composed of atypical basaloid cells with limited cytoplasm
